detail:
MedlinePlus describes premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) as a condition marked by severe depressed mood symptoms, irritability, and tension before menstruation, with symptoms more severe than those seen with premenstrual syndrome (PMS). The encyclopedia notes that PMS refers to a wide range of physical or emotional symptoms that most often occur about 5 to 11 days before a menstrual cycle starts, and that PMDD affects a small number of women during the years when they are having menstrual periods. The causes of PMS and PMDD have not been found, according to the source.

MedlinePlus notes that symptoms can include depressed mood, anxiety and tension, mood swings, irritability, difficulty concentrating, fatigue, changes in appetite and sleep, and physical symptoms such as breast tenderness, bloating, and headaches. The source notes that no physical exam or lab test can diagnose PMDD, and that evaluation generally involves a complete history, a physical exam, thyroid testing, and assessment for other conditions that could explain the symptoms.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about premenstrual dysphoric disorder symptoms and diagnosis.
summary: MedlinePlus explains PMDD as a severe premenstrual condition marked by depressed mood, irritability, and tension, more severe than PMS, with no single exam or lab test for diagnosis.
takeaways: PMDD is more severe than PMS and centers on mood symptoms
symptoms can include irritability, tension, and depressed mood before menstruation
no physical exam or lab test diagnoses PMDD on its own
title: PMDD (Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder): severe premenstrual mood symptoms
